title: Small leftovers: navigation docs and schedule page limits
request: Doug said: do all of these. (1) Close the old ready task T-261030-unit-test-for-an-unteste. (2) iPhone check of PLAYOFF-43. (3) navigation.md routes table omits /recap/:seasonSlug/:week and /join. (4) navigation.md says scroll is never reset but ScrollToTop is mounted. (5) The small schedule-page limits left by the polish task: keyboard pager under the sticky bar on one Tab path, the focus ring cut on the outer side of the first and last date chip, the Add reaction 30px button, the 43px team links, the load jump.

criteria.text: Docs: the navigation routes table lists every route in App.tsx except the dev-only proof route and the counts agree; no page or row still says a link keeps the old scroll position; the scroll-restore finding is recorded as an open question and in B-14; totals recounted
criteria.evidence: Routes table checked row by row against src/App.tsx and routeReachability.test.ts: 24 named routes (added /recap/:seasonSlug/:week, /join, /forgot-password, /reset-password); counts now twenty-four; the six never-in-a-menu routes match the test. Scroll measured in a real browser on the dev server and the production build (before/scroll-check-out.txt, scroll-matrix-prod-out.txt, scroll-matrix-wide2-out.txt, scroll-matrix-team-out.txt, scroll-reload-prod-out.txt): a link resets scroll (337 -> 0 on both builds); Back and Forward landed at 0 on /schedule, /teams, /history, /insights and on /stats after a top-bar link; /stats after a team page restored 300 of 300; a probe showed the saved /stats position overwritten with 0 as the page was left; a reload keeps scroll on /stats, /teams, /history. About 20 pages and 18 rows rewritten, the finding recorded as an open question, under B-14 and as suspected-bug marks on NAV-02, BROWSE-04, BROWSE-37, TEAM-33 and PHONE-22 (NAV-01 lost its mark). Recount by the README method: 1958 items, 120 P1 suspected-bug rows (was 116). Not fixed on purpose: the scroll restore itself is a product bug, not decided.

criteria.text: (a) The tab panel stop no longer hides the pager row under the sticky bar: overlap 60 -> 0 on the phone, nothing worse on desktop (real browser, before/after)
criteria.evidence: Keyboard walk at 390x844, before/tabwalk-390-upcoming.txt vs after/tabwalk-390-upcoming-after.txt (production build): the tab panel stop was top 0 with 60 of 60 px under the sticky bar, now top 64 with 0 hidden, and the sweep from scroll 0 to 200 shows the same. Desktop 1280: panel top 97, overlap 0, and 6 overlap lines before and 6 after (the left-alone Shift+Tab team links), so nothing worse. The three TabsContent carry scroll-mt-16 (computed 64px).

criteria.text: (b) The focus ring is whole on the first and last date chip, including when the selected date is the first or last chip; chip widths unchanged; no neighbour sliver; the move of the chips is measured and stated
criteria.evidence: Ring pixel diff (audit2/ring2.mjs) with the selected date middle, first and last, at 390 and 1280: before (production build of the old code, before/ring-before-prod.txt) the first and last chip had 0 to 2 px of room, and with the selected date first or last the ring was cut to one column at the left and zero at the right; after (after/ring-after-dev.txt) room is 6 px each side and the full ring pattern shows in all three cases. Chip widths unchanged (50 px phone, 52.6 desktop), box edges unchanged (4..386 and 20..1260) so no neighbour sliver; the chips sit 4 px further in (phone x 6 -> 10, desktop 22 -> 26). Pixel diff of full-page shots at 390 and 1280, Upcoming and Completed (after/pixdiff.txt, after/diff-crops.png): only the strip rows, the Add reaction button, and clock text (Updated time, minutes until match) differ.

criteria.text: (c) Add reaction is 44x44 on the phone and 30x44 on desktop; (d) team links are shown to be 44px already, no change
criteria.evidence: Tap targets (audit2/targets.mjs, before/targets-prod.txt vs after/targets-prod.txt): Add reaction 30 x 44 -> 44 x 44 on the phone, 30 x 44 unchanged on desktop. Team links already 44 px tall on both widths (logo 44 x 44, names 44 x 87..120); the 43 was getBoundingClientRect read during the animate-scale-in start, offsetHeight 44 throughout. No change made for the team links.

criteria.text: (e) The Completed tab cards no longer shrink 84px when comments arrive and the date strip is 76px from the first paint; the parts not fixed (division chips, Updated row, prediction bar, footer) are named
criteria.evidence: Load jump (audit2/completedgrow.mjs with the comments delayed 700 ms, and load2.mjs with every answer delayed 300 ms): Completed card 326 px then 242 px (an 84 px shrink) -> 242 px from the first paint, page height identical when loaded; date strip 68 px then 76 px (an 8 px jump when the dots arrive) -> 76 px from the first paint. Not fixed, named in the commits: division chip pop-in (+52 px), Updated row (+52 px), prediction bar pop-in (about +60 px a card), the app-wide footer shift. Total layout shift score is about the same, 0.2532 before and 0.2559 after, because the footer shift (0.20) dominates; so the fix removes two visible jumps and does not make the page steady.

criteria.text: Six checks pass at the final head; changed tests edited to match, none skipped or loosened; docs and the DateStrip comment say what the code does; links 0 broken
criteria.evidence: All six required checks pass at the final code and docs commit cbe00dd: integrity, typecheck, lint, knip, build, unit (826 files, 7530 tests; was 826 and 7524). Changed and new tests only add exact class checks (scroll-mt-16 on the three tab panels, px-1.5 and after:w-0.5 and after:shrink-0 on the strip row, min-h-16 on chips with and without a dot, min-w-11 and md:min-w-0 on Add reaction, the single h-11 skeleton); the builder showed the 7 new or strengthened tests fail on the old source. No skip, only, todo, ts-expect-error or eslint-disable added. Links: 2735 checked, 0 broken.

reviews.summary: Independent plan review of the schedule fixes: a, c, d, e can go ahead; b needs more room and one more test. (b) The selected date becomes the first or last chip whenever it is more than 3 days back or 10 days ahead (DateStrip.tsx:40-41), and the selected chip is scale-105, so its ring sticks out about 5.45px; px-1 gives 4px on the left and 5px on the right, so about 1.45px stays cut, and the audit never tested selected-and-first. Use px-1.5 and after:w-0.5 (gap 4 + 2 = 6px) and run the ring pixel diff with the selected day first and last. The spacer comment must say 5px or 6px of room, not 1px. (a) fine; the desktop claim is unproven (both 1280 walks show no overlap before or after), drop it. (c) matches the house pattern (ScheduleFilters.tsx:57, Q14); add a short comment citing it; emoji chips 39-43px are left alone. (d) not reproducible, no change. (e) both one-liners right; strengthen the skeleton test to expect the h-11 class. Docs: only the DateStrip comment needs rewording.

Independent reviewer, four rounds, final APPROVE at cbe00dd (docs, last confirmation) over the four code commits. Round 1: code APPROVE-quality (Tailwind v4 classes confirmed in the built CSS, new tests assert exact classes and fail without them, no skip or only or todo or ts-expect-error or eslint-disable, no assertion loosened, evidence supports the commit messages) but CHANGES on docs: A11Y-03 and accessibility.md still said the new page does not scroll to the top, team-details still said Back to /teams restores scroll in bold, the playoffs footer did not name B-14, plus reload-keeps-scroll, team Back via navigate(-1), deep links, wording. All verified against the code and fixed. Round 2: one more stale passage (past-seasons said navigation.md called /teams the only restoring route) and nits, fixed. Round 3 at cbe00dd: APPROVE, fresh-term sweep found nothing, recount 1958 items and 120 suspected-bug rows, links 0 broken. The reviewer re-measured scroll on the production preview and agreed. Stated limits: the load jump is only partly fixed (total shift score about 0.253 before and 0.256 after; the footer and the filter chips are left alone); at 390 wide four different emoji now wrap the reaction row; desktop Chromium only, no iPhone.
